## Annotation

Mowat, speaking as an MLA in support of the budget, describes Pearson Hospital as an extended-care setting whose average age is 42, and names “a new type of disabled person called a high-lesion respiratory quadriplegic.” He then states that six such persons “will soon be leaving Pearson Hospital to move into their own accommodation at the Creekview Co-op on False Creek,” into “a six-bedroom co-op apartment … with all the support services plugged in.” He contrasts a Pearson per diem of $300 (about $2,000 a day for the six) with an estimated $45 to $50 per diem in the co-op. He frames the move as “mainstreaming.”

This is the earliest public official text inspected in this pass that names Creekview as the destination for ventilator-dependent high-lesion quadriplegia leaving Pearson. It is **pre-opening**: “will soon be leaving.” It does not use the numeral “202,” does not name an evaluation, and does not name CSIL or ECPM.

`source_type` is `primary`: a contemporaneous legislative record of a planned move, not a later summary.

## Limitations

- Cost figures and the “six-bedroom” description are Mowat’s 1984 estimates, not an inspected evaluation.
- The HTML banner states that the printed Hansard remains official.
- Later sources date opening to September 1985 ([Haw 1989](1989-haw-special-housing-needs.qmd); [SCI BC history](sci-bc-history.qmd)). This sitting does not give an opening date.

## Open questions

- Whether “Creekview Co-op on False Creek” is the same legal entity later called Creekview 202 / Creekview Cooperative Apartment.
- How Mowat obtained the per-diem figures (ministry briefing, CPA, or personal knowledge).
- Whether Hansard after opening (see [Nielsen, 10 April 1986](1986-hansard-nielsen-creekview.qmd)) describes the same six residents.
